| Form                             | Example                              | Matching                                                                                        |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| CSS                              | `button[type=submit]`, `css=.card a` | Selector query. Also searches open shadow roots.                                                |
| `@e` reference                   | `@e<generation>.<index>`             | A node from the latest `snapshot`.                                                              |
| `role=`                          | `role=button[name="Submit"]`         | Accessibility role and optional name. The name is a JSON string and matches exactly.            |
| `text=`                          | `text=Sign in`, `text="Sign in"`     | Rendered text. Unquoted values match a case-insensitive substring; quoted values match exactly. |
| `label=`                         | `label=Email`                        | The associated label text or `aria-label`.                                                      |
| `placeholder=`, `alt=`, `title=` | `placeholder=Search`                 | The matching attribute.                                                                         |
| `testid=`                        | `testid=search`                      | The `data-testid` attribute.                                                                    |
| `xpath=`                         | `xpath=//table//a`                   | XPath in the current document only. Shadow roots are not traversed.                             |

Append ` >>nth=0` to take the first match or ` >>nth=-1` to take the last. Text, CSS and attribute locators traverse open shadow roots. Closed shadow roots stay invisible to them.

## Reference lifetime [#reference-lifetime]

`@e` references belong to one document generation. In Chrome, a new snapshot, a frame selection, a new main document (navigation or reload) or a change of the tab's URL invalidates them. A snapshot taken inside a selected frame also expires when that frame navigates, reloads, is removed, or the selection ends. Other iframes loading or navigating leave it valid. In Firefox, references live in the document that produced them; see [Firefox](https://oh-my-webbridge.github.io/en/firefox/).

## Errors [#errors]

Every fault carries `code` and `message`. The HTTP status is shown below; a code not listed here returns 502.

| Code                    | HTTP | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                   | What to do                                                                                             |
| ----------------------- | ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `invalid_request`       | 400  | The body was rejected: an unknown field, a missing action or session, a session name outside the allowed characters, a bad `browser`, or `timeoutMs` outside 1 to 120000. | Fix the JSON. The message names the field.                                                             |
| `invalid_args`          | 400  | An argument is missing, has the wrong type, or is outside its range.                                                                                                      | Read the message; it names the action and argument.                                                    |
| `unsupported`           | 501  | The action or one of its arguments does not exist in the target browser.                                                                                                  | Do not retry. Use another action, or a Chrome session.                                                 |
| `busy`                  | 429  | A capacity limit is full: command slots, 32 tabs per session, 128 sessions per browser, the Firefox upload budget, or two concurrent artifact jobs.                       | Reduce concurrency and retry after earlier commands finish.                                            |
| `browser_offline`       | 503  | The target browser has no extension connection, including a session bound to a browser that is not connected.                                                             | Check `omw doctor` and the extension, or continue in a new session.                                    |
| `session_browser`       | 409  | The session is bound to the other browser and the request named this one.                                                                                                 | Drop `browser`, or close the session and start a new one.                                              |
| `outcome_unknown`       | 504  | The command may have run: the deadline, a transport write or a disconnect cut off the reply.                                                                              | Observe the page or network state before repeating. Never replay a submit, payment or publish blindly. |
| `tab_busy`              | 409  | The tab belongs to another session.                                                                                                                                       | Use a tab this session holds, or another session.                                                      |
| `stale_ref`             | 409  | An `@e` reference outlived its document.                                                                                                                                  | Take a new `snapshot`.                                                                                 |
| `no_tab`                | 502  | A page action ran before the session had a tab.                                                                                                                           | Run `navigate` or `find_tab` first.                                                                    |
| `tab_missing`           | 502  | `find_tab` matched no tab.                                                                                                                                                | Open the page in this session first, or pass `active: true` to borrow the browser's active tab.        |
| `restricted_tab`        | 502  | The tab is not a normal, non-incognito HTTP(S) page.                                                                                                                      | Navigate to an HTTP(S) page. Browser-internal pages are not scriptable.                                |
| `borrowed_tab`          | 502  | The action needs a tab the session created: closing it, or applying a preset to a borrowed tab.                                                                           | Open a task tab with `navigate`.                                                                       |
| `element_missing`       | 502  | The selector matched nothing.                                                                                                                                             | Check the selector, or take a new snapshot.                                                            |
| `element_hidden`        | 502  | The element has no box, so it has no center to click.                                                                                                                     | Scroll it into view or wait for it to render.                                                          |
| `element_action_failed` | 502  | The page refused the operation, such as filling a non-editable element or selecting an option that does not exist.                                                        | Inspect with `get` or `is` and adjust the action.                                                      |
| `state_mismatch`        | 502  | `check` or `uncheck` left the control in the wrong state.                                                                                                                 | Re-read it with `is`, then retry or click it instead.                                                  |
| `evaluation_failed`     | 502  | `evaluate` threw, or an internal page script did.                                                                                                                         | Fix the expression. The message carries the page exception.                                            |
| `frame_missing`         | 502  | `frame` found no frame for the given selector, id, name or URL.                                                                                                           | List frames with `frame {"cmd":"list"}` and select one.                                                |
| `frame_unavailable`     | 502  | The selected frame was replaced, removed or lost its execution context.                                                                                                   | Later commands use the main frame; select the frame again if the work continues there.                 |
| `history_missing`       | 502  | `history back` or `forward` has no entry in that direction.                                                                                                               | Read `history {"cmd":"list"}` first.                                                                   |
| `request_missing`       | 502  | No network record exists for the request, or it was evicted.                                                                                                              | Start recording, reproduce, then read `list`.                                                          |
| `request_pending`       | 502  | The response body is not complete yet.                                                                                                                                    | Wait for `complete: true` in `list`, then retry `detail`.                                              |
| `request_failed`        | 502  | The request itself failed.                                                                                                                                                | Read the error text on the entry.                                                                      |
| `download_missing`      | 502  | The browser does not list the download.                                                                                                                                   | Retry the `download`.                                                                                  |
| `download_failed`       | 502  | The browser interrupted the download.                                                                                                                                     | Read the message and retry.                                                                            |
| `window_failed`         | 502  | The new window had no tab.                                                                                                                                                | Retry `window_new`.                                                                                    |
| `result_too_large`      | 502  | A result exceeded 32 MiB on the wire, or a network body exceeded 2 Mi characters in Chrome or 1 MiB in Firefox.                                                           | Narrow the result: use `selector` or `jpeg` for screenshots, and read smaller pieces.                  |
| `debugger_unavailable`  | 502  | Chrome refused the debugger attach, for example because DevTools is open or policy blocks it.                                                                             | Close DevTools for that tab and retry.                                                                 |
| `browser_error`         | 502  | The extension reported an error without a code.                                                                                                                           | Read the message, retry once, then report it.                                                          |
| `internal`              | 502  | A daemon-side failure, such as encoding a request.                                                                                                                        | Retry. If it persists, restart the daemon.                                                             |


# CDP (https://oh-my-webbridge.github.io/en/reference/cdp/)

The daemon exposes Chrome DevTools Protocol in two modes at `127.0.0.1:17373`, the same address and port as the rest of its API:

- **Extension mode** serves page targets through `chrome.debugger` in the Chrome extension. It needs a paired Chrome extension and works with the browser profile you already have open.
- **Native mode** is a WebSocket proxy to a Chrome browser endpoint you start with remote debugging. It is enabled with `omw serve --cdp`.

Every request needs `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, including WebSocket upgrades. Get the token with `omw connection`. The `Host` header must be `127.0.0.1`. Requests that carry a web `Origin` are rejected with 403.

## Endpoints in extension mode [#endpoints-in-extension-mode]

| Endpoint                 | Method    | Reply                                             |
| ------------------------ | --------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `/json`, `/json/list`    | GET       | The open page targets, as a JSON array.           |
| `/json/version`          | GET       | A version object without a browser WebSocket URL. |
| `/devtools/page/{tabId}` | WebSocket | One CDP session for one tab.                      |

When only the Firefox extension is connected, these endpoints answer HTTP 501 with the error code `unsupported`. When no browser is connected, `/json` and `/json/list` answer HTTP 503, while `/json/version` still returns its object.

### /json/list [#jsonlist]

```sh
TOKEN=$(omw connection | sed -E 's/.*"token":"([^"]+)".*/\1/')
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://127.0.0.1:17373/json/list
```

```json
[
  {
    "id": "123456789",
    "type": "page",
    "url": "https://example.com/",
    "title": "Example Domain",
    "webSocketDebuggerUrl": "ws://127.0.0.1:17373/devtools/page/123456789"
  }
]
```

`id` is the tab id. The list covers non-incognito HTTP(S) and `about:blank` tabs that belong to sessions and tabs you opened, because the extension can attach to both.

### /json/version [#jsonversion]

```json
{
  "Browser": "oh-my-webbridge/0.2.0",
  "Protocol-Version": "1.3",
  "User-Agent": "oh-my-webbridge",
  "transport": "chrome.debugger (page targets only)"
}
```

The object has no `webSocketDebuggerUrl`, so a client that discovers targets through `/json/version` finds none in this mode.

## Page connections [#page-connections]

Connect to `ws://127.0.0.1:17373/devtools/page/{tabId}` with the Bearer header on the upgrade request. Before the WebSocket is accepted, the daemon asks the extension to attach to that tab.

- A tab another session is using answers HTTP 409 and is not taken over.
- The tab is released when the client disconnects, when the tab closes, when the debugger detaches, and when the daemon stops or the extension pauses or disconnects. Clients can reconnect afterwards.
- Events for the tab are subscribed before the attach starts, so events that arrive before the attach reply are still forwarded.

Messages use the CDP shape. Commands need `id` and `method`:

```json
{ "id": 1, "method": "Page.navigate", "params": { "url": "https://example.com/" } }
```

A reply carries `result`, or an error object with code `-32000`:

```json
{ "id": 1, "error": { "code": -32000, "message": "..." } }
```

Events carry `method`, `params` and, when the event belongs to a child target, `sessionId`. Replies can arrive out of order; the original ids are preserved.

Limits on one page connection:

| Limit                | Value      |
| -------------------- | ---------- |
| Commands in flight   | 32         |
| Deadline per command | 30 seconds |
| Message size         | 32 MiB     |

An event larger than 32 MiB is not forwarded. The bridge emits `Inspector.detached` for that tab and closes the connection. The daemon also closes the connection for an event whose parameters exceed 256 KiB. A client that cannot keep up with the event stream is disconnected rather than silently losing events.

When the page reports `Inspector.detached` without a `sessionId`, the daemon forwards it and closes the WebSocket, which matches the behavior of Chrome's own page endpoint.

## The cdp action [#the-cdp-action]

The `cdp` action sends one protocol command on the session's current tab, attaching the tab if needed. It is the same transport as a page connection, without the WebSocket.

```sh
omw call research cdp '{"method":"Page.navigate","params":{"url":"https://example.com/"}}'
```

```js
import { connect } from "./dist/sdk.mjs";

const task = await connect("research");
const { frameTree } = await task.cdp("Page.getFrameTree");
```

| Argument    | Type     | Meaning                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `method`    | `string` | Protocol method, for example `Page.navigate`.                                                                                                         |
| `params`    | `object` | Method parameters. Defaults to `{}`.                                                                                                                  |
| `sessionId` | `string` | Child target session, for a flat session opened by `Target.attachToTarget` with `flatten: true`. Omitted, the command goes to the tab's root session. |

The action is available in Chrome only. Firefox answers `unsupported` with HTTP 501 and the message `cdp is not available in Firefox: Firefox has no Chrome DevTools Protocol`.

Two methods interact with the rest of the bridge:

- `Page.disable` on the root session clears the `@e` references of that tab. The next `snapshot` or `navigate` enables Page events again.
- `Runtime.disable` ends the frame selection of that session. Later commands run in the main frame until `frame` selects one again.

## Native mode [#native-mode]

```sh
omw serve --cdp ws://127.0.0.1:9222/devtools/browser/8b0d3f7c-...
```

The URL must start with `ws://` or `wss://` and include a host. Otherwise the daemon refuses to start. Start Chrome with `--remote-debugging-port=9222` to get that URL from `http://127.0.0.1:9222/json/version`.

In native mode, `/json/version` adds the browser WebSocket URL and reports the other transport:

```json
{
  "Browser": "oh-my-webbridge/0.2.0",
  "Protocol-Version": "1.3",
  "User-Agent": "oh-my-webbridge",
  "transport": "native CDP passthrough",
  "webSocketDebuggerUrl": "ws://127.0.0.1:17373/devtools/browser"
}
```

`/devtools/browser` opens a WebSocket to that URL and copies frames in both directions, so every CDP domain and every browser-level target is available. It answers HTTP 503 while native mode is not configured (501 while only the Firefox extension is connected), and HTTP 502 when the configured endpoint cannot be reached. The upstream dial has a 10 second timeout.

Playwright can connect to the proxy:

```js
import { chromium } from "playwright-core";

const browser = await chromium.connectOverCDP("http://127.0.0.1:17373", {
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.OMW_TOKEN}` },
});
```

Set `OMW_TOKEN` to the `token` value from `omw connection`. Playwright reads `/json/version` and uses the `webSocketDebuggerUrl` it finds.

Native mode does not replace extension mode. `/json/list` still lists targets through the Chrome extension, so without the Chrome extension it answers HTTP 503 (501 while only the Firefox extension is connected) even when the proxy works.

## Limits [#limits]

- Extension mode carries page targets only. The browser target endpoint is not available, and the domains Chrome allows to `chrome.debugger` are a subset of the full protocol. See the [`chrome.debugger` reference](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/api/debugger) for that list.
- Native mode forwards whatever the configured endpoint accepts; the daemon does not filter domains or methods.
- Chrome does not accept `--remote-debugging-port` together with the default profile directory in current versions. Point it at a separate user data directory; see [remote debugging](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/remote-debugging-port).
- CDP replies, events and the `cdp` action's result share the 32 MiB message limit of the rest of the bridge. The action's arguments, like any `/command` body, are limited to 2 MiB.


# CLI (https://oh-my-webbridge.github.io/en/reference/cli/)

`omw` is the Go daemon and its command line client. It listens on `127.0.0.1:17373` and has no option to bind another address or a network interface. `serve` and `start` run the daemon. `stop`, `status`, `doctor`, `pair` and `call` need one already running. `connection`, `skill`, `install-skill`, `service install`, `version` and `help` work without it.

| Command               | Purpose                                                     |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `omw serve`           | Run the daemon in the foreground.                           |
| `omw start`           | Start a background daemon; safe to run when one is running. |
| `omw stop`            | Stop the daemon and leave tabs open.                        |
| `omw status`          | Print the daemon status and one line per browser.           |
| `omw doctor`          | Same as `status`, plus the configuration path.              |
| `omw pair`            | Print a pairing code for a browser extension.               |
| `omw connection`      | Print the endpoint, token and protocol version.             |
| `omw call`            | Send one action to a session.                               |
| `omw service install` | Install a launchd or systemd user service.                  |
| `omw install-skill`   | Write the bundled agent guide below a directory.            |
| `omw skill`           | Print the bundled agent guide.                              |
| `omw version`         | Print the daemon version.                                   |
| `omw help`            | Print the command list.                                     |

Every command exits with status 0 on success. On failure it prints `omw: ` and the error to stderr, then exits with status 1.

## serve [#serve]

```sh
omw serve [--cdp ws://127.0.0.1:9222/devtools/browser/...]
```

Runs the daemon in the foreground until SIGINT or SIGTERM. The listener is fixed at `127.0.0.1:17373`. If `config.json` names another address, the daemon refuses to start.

`--cdp` points the daemon at a Chrome browser endpoint already running with remote debugging. The URL must start with `ws://` or `wss://` and carry a host. With this flag, `/devtools/browser` proxies that endpoint; see [CDP](https://oh-my-webbridge.github.io/en/reference/cdp/#native-mode).

The endpoint is not written to `config.json`. A `cdp` field already present in that file is read at startup, and the flag replaces it for that process.

## start [#start]

```sh
omw start
```

Starts `omw serve` in a new session, detached from the terminal, with `OMW_HOME` set to the configuration directory. Output goes to `daemon.log` in that directory. The file is emptied on every start. The command waits about two seconds for the daemon to answer `/status`.

It prints `started` on success and `already running` when the daemon answers on the port. When another process holds the port, or the token does not match, it reports a port or credential mismatch and exits with status 1. When the new daemon does not answer in that window, it prints the contents of `daemon.log`.

## stop [#stop]

```sh
omw stop
```

Sends `POST /shutdown` and prints the reply, `{"stopping":true}`. Tabs that sessions opened stay open. Bindings in `bindings.json` are kept.

## status and doctor [#status-and-doctor]

```sh
omw status
omw doctor
```

Both print the daemon's `/status` JSON to stdout and one line per browser to stderr:

```text
chrome: connected (156.0.8078.80)
firefox: not connected
```

`doctor` adds the path of `config.json` to stderr before those lines.

`status` is an authenticated request. Without a running daemon it exits with status 1 and the connection error.

## pair [#pair]

```sh
omw pair
```

Asks the daemon for a pairing code and prints it in two groups of three digits:

```text
Enter this code in the oh-my-webbridge extension:

    482 913

It works once and expires in 5 minutes.
```

The code is valid for 5 minutes and 5 attempts. The command polls the daemon every 500 ms and prints `Paired with Chrome.` or `Paired with Firefox.` when the extension redeems the code. It exits with status 1 when the code expires. Without a running daemon it prints the hint to run `omw start`.

## connection [#connection]

```sh
omw connection
```

Prints one JSON object:

```json
{
  "endpoint": "ws://127.0.0.1:17373/extension",
  "token": "64 hex characters",
  "protocol": 1
}
```

The token is 32 random bytes in hex, the same value that `config.json` holds. It authorizes every request other than `GET /ping` and `POST /pair`, including WebSocket upgrades and CDP connections. Treat it as a secret: do not paste it into issues, logs or pages.

## call [#call]

```sh
omw call [--browser chrome|firefox] SESSION ACTION [JSON|-]
```

Sends one action to the daemon and prints its JSON reply. The session name is 1 to 96 letters (including CJK), digits, `_`, `.` or `-`. `ACTION` is one of the actions in the [action reference](https://oh-my-webbridge.github.io/en/reference/actions/).

The optional third argument is a JSON object with the action arguments. With `-`, the command reads that object from stdin, up to 2 MiB. Without it, the daemon receives `{}`.

```sh
omw call research navigate '{"url":"https://example.com/"}'
echo '{"selector":"#submit"}' | omw call --browser firefox form click -
```

`--browser` sends the action to the named browser. Without it the daemon routes by the session binding, then the only connected browser, then Chrome.

The client waits up to 125 seconds. The daemon applies the command's own deadline, which defaults to 30 seconds. The reply is printed as the daemon sends it. An HTTP status of 400 or above makes the command exit with status 1 after printing the reply.

## service install [#service-install]

```sh
omw service install
```

Installs a user service that runs `omw serve` at login, with `OMW_HOME` set to the configuration directory the command used.

| Platform | File                                               | Activation                                                                                     |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| macOS    | `~/Library/LaunchAgents/app.oh-my-webbridge.plist` | `launchctl bootstrap gui/$UID`                                                                 |
| Linux    | `~/.config/systemd/user/oh-my-webbridge.service`   | `systemctl --user daemon-reload`, then `systemctl --user enable --now oh-my-webbridge.service` |

The service keeps the daemon running: `KeepAlive` on macOS, `Restart=on-failure` with a 3 second delay on Linux. Output is discarded on macOS; the systemd unit keeps the default journal.

## install-skill and skill [#install-skill-and-skill]

```sh
omw install-skill DIRECTORY
omw skill
```

`install-skill` writes the bundled agent guide to `DIRECTORY/oh-my-webbridge/SKILL.md` with mode 0600, and creates the directory with mode 0700. It refuses to overwrite an existing file.

`skill` prints the same guide to stdout.

```sh
omw install-skill ~/.agents/skills
```

## version and help [#version-and-help]

```sh
omw version
omw --version
omw help
```

`version` prints the daemon version. `help`, `--help` and a bare `omw` print the command list.

An unknown command prints `omw: unknown command "NAME"; run omw help` and exits with status 1.

## Configuration directory [#configuration-directory]

The directory is resolved in this order:

1. `OMW_HOME`, when set.
2. macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/oh-my-webbridge`.
3. Linux: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/oh-my-webbridge`, or `~/.config/oh-my-webbridge` when `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is unset.

The CLI, the daemon, the user service and the [SDK](https://oh-my-webbridge.github.io/en/reference/sdk/) all read the same directory. Every command that reads the configuration creates it with mode 0700 when it is missing.

| File            | Contents                                                                                                     |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `config.json`   | `token` (64 hex characters), `address`, and an optional `cdp` endpoint. Created with mode 0600 on first use. |
| `bindings.json` | Session to browser bindings, mode 0600, read at startup.                                                     |
| `daemon.log`    | Output of the daemon started by `omw start`, emptied on every start.                                         |
| `artifacts/`    | Screenshots and PDFs saved without an explicit `path`.                                                       |

The token in `config.json` is the only credential. Anyone who reads the file can drive the paired browsers, so keep the directory private and do not copy `config.json` between machines.


# JavaScript SDK (https://oh-my-webbridge.github.io/en/reference/sdk/)

The SDK is one module, `sdk/index.ts`, built to `dist/sdk.mjs` by `pnpm run build`. It is an ESM module for Node.js 24 and later. It reads `config.json` from the [configuration directory](https://oh-my-webbridge.github.io/en/reference/cli/#configuration-directory) and sends actions to `POST /command`.

`connect` returns a task object bound to one session name. The extension opens that session's tabs and tab group on demand, as it does for `omw call`.

```js
import { connect } from "./dist/sdk.mjs";

const task = await connect("research");
await task.navigate("https://example.com/");
const page = await task.evaluate("({title:document.title,url:location.href})");
console.log(page.title);
await task.close();
```

## connect(session, options) [#connectsession-options]

```ts
const task = await connect("research", { browser: "firefox" });
```

| Argument          | Type                    | Meaning                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `session`         | `string`                | Session name: 1 to 96 letters (including CJK), digits, `_`, `.` or `-`. Validated by the daemon.                                      |
| `options.browser` | `"chrome" \| "firefox"` | Sends every command to this browser. Omitted, the daemon routes by the session binding, then the only connected browser, then Chrome. |

`connect` rejects when:

- `config.json` is missing or unreadable. Run `omw start` first; it creates the file.
- `address` in the file is not `127.0.0.1:17373`; the message is `unsupported daemon address`.
- `browser` is another string; the message is `unsupported browser: safari`.

The returned object has `session`, `browser` (undefined when no browser was given), and the methods below.

## Task methods [#task-methods]

| Method                            | Sends                | Resolves with                                                                                |
| --------------------------------- | -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `call(action, args, options)`     | `action` with `args` | The command result, untyped unless you pass a type argument.                                 |
| `navigate(url, newTab = false)`   | `navigate`           | `{ success, tabId, url }`                                                                    |
| `preset(preset, options)`         | `preset`             | `{ config, tabs }` with the state of each task tab. `options` takes `zen` and `environment`. |
| `snapshot()`                      | `snapshot`           | `{ tree, truncated, url, title }`                                                            |
| `click(selector)`                 | `click`              | `{ success: true }`                                                                          |
| `fill(selector, value)`           | `fill`               | `{ success: true }`                                                                          |
| `evaluate(code)`                  | `evaluate`           | The expression value, not the wrapper object.                                                |
| `cdp(method, params, sessionId?)` | `cdp`                | The CDP command result.                                                                      |
| `close()`                         | `close_session`      | `{ success, closed }` with the number of closed tabs.                                        |

`evaluate` runs a JavaScript expression in the page. Wrap asynchronous code in an IIFE:

```js
const count = await task.evaluate("(async () => (await fetch('/api/count')).text())()");
```

```js
const links = await task.evaluate("document.querySelectorAll('a').length");
```

Selectors accept the forms listed in the [action reference](https://oh-my-webbridge.github.io/en/reference/actions/#selectors), including CSS, `@e` references from a snapshot, `role=`, `text=` and `xpath=`.

## call(action, args, options) [#callaction-args-options]

```ts
const result = await task.call(
  "get",
  { selector: "#price", property: "text" },
  { timeoutMs: 5000 },
);
```

| Option      | Type          | Default | Meaning                                                                                    |
| ----------- | ------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `timeoutMs` | `number`      | `30000` | Deadline for the command, including its time in the queue. The daemon accepts 1 to 120000. |
| `signal`    | `AbortSignal` | none    | Cancels the request. It is combined with an internal timeout of `timeoutMs + 5000`.        |

The request is aborted locally 5 seconds after the daemon deadline. That gives the daemon time to answer with `outcome_unknown` when the page did not finish.

```js
const controller = new AbortController();
setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 2000);
try {
  await task.call("wait", { selector: "#done", state: "visible" }, { signal: controller.signal });
} catch (error) {
  console.log(error.name);
}
```

## Errors [#errors]

A rejected call is an `Error` with a `code` property. When the daemon answers with a command error, `code` and `message` are the daemon's `error.code` and `error.message`.

```js
try {
  await task.click("@e12");
} catch (error) {
  if (error.code === "stale_ref") {
    await task.snapshot();
  } else {
    throw error;
  }
}
```

| `code`                                     | Cause                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `stale_ref`, `tab_busy`, `session_browser` | The reference expired, another session holds the tab, or the session is bound to another browser. HTTP 409.                          |
| `browser_offline`                          | The target browser has no connected extension. HTTP 503.                                                                             |
| `unsupported`                              | The action or argument is not available in that browser. HTTP 501.                                                                   |
| `busy`                                     | Command capacity is full. HTTP 429. Retry after a running command finishes.                                                          |
| `outcome_unknown`                          | The command may have taken effect. Read the page before retrying. HTTP 504.                                                          |
| `invalid_args`, `invalid_request`          | The arguments were rejected before dispatch. HTTP 400.                                                                               |
| `http_error`                               | The reply was not JSON, so the daemon's error object is missing. The message is `HTTP <status>: <first 200 characters of the body>`. |

The request never reached the command handler when the reply has no JSON content type. Causes: a rejected token, a non-loopback `Host`, a web `Origin`, or another service on port 17373.

An aborted request rejects with an `AbortError` and no daemon fault code. A refused connection rejects with the `fetch` `TypeError`.

The full list of codes and recovery steps is in the [action reference](https://oh-my-webbridge.github.io/en/reference/actions/#errors).

## Parallel tasks [#parallel-tasks]

Each session owns its tabs. Give every task its own session name, then start them together with `Promise.all`. The daemon runs the commands concurrently, up to 128 in flight per browser.

```js
import { connect } from "./dist/sdk.mjs";

const tasks = [
  { session: "chrome-docs", url: "https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/" },
  { session: "go-docs", url: "https://go.dev/doc/" },
];

const results = await Promise.all(
  tasks.map(async ({ session, url }) => {
    const task = await connect(session);
    try {
      await task.navigate(url);
      const page = await task.evaluate("({title:document.title,url:location.href})");
      return { session, ...page };
    } finally {
      await task.close();
    }
  }),
);

console.log(JSON.stringify(results, null, 2));
```

```json
[
  {
    "session": "chrome-docs",
    "title": "Chrome Extensions documentation",
    "url": "https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/"
  },
  {
    "session": "go-docs",
    "title": "The Go Programming Language",
    "url": "https://go.dev/doc/"
  }
]
```

Two tasks with the same session name share their tabs and CDP state, so give independent work distinct names.

Closing a task closes the tabs the session opened, releases borrowed tabs and deletes the session binding. When `close` is not called, the tabs stay open and the binding is kept, so a later `connect` with the same name resumes the session.

## Types [#types]

`sdk/index.ts` imports `Args`, `Browser`, `Json` and `Fault` from the extension protocol. `call` accepts a type parameter for the result:

```ts
const box = await task.call<{ x: number; y: number }>("get", {
  selector: "#cart",
  property: "box",
});
```


# Sessions and tabs (https://oh-my-webbridge.github.io/en/sessions/)

A session is the unit of work in oh-my-webbridge. Every command names a session, and the daemon routes it to the tabs that session holds. Tabs opened by a session sit in a tab group titled with the session name or the title the agent passed, so a task's pages stay together and apart from the pages you use.

<Demo
  name="activity-read"
  alt="Session demo reads an article in the tab it opened: the page scrolls from section to section, and the chip in the corner names the session."
/>

## One session per task [#one-session-per-task]

Give each task its own session name and reuse it for everything the task does. Tasks that run at the same time use different names. Each session keeps its own tabs, tab group, current tab, presets and frame selection. The browser runs commands from different sessions at the same time.

```sh
omw call research navigate '{"url":"https://example.com/docs","group_title":"Research"}'
omw call billing navigate '{"url":"https://example.com/pricing","group_title":"Billing"}'
```

A session starts with its first command. Its name is 1 to 96 letters (including CJK), digits, `_`, `.` or `-`.

## A session stays in one browser [#a-session-stays-in-one-browser]

A session's first command decides the browser it stays in: the browser named by `browser`, the only connected browser, or Chrome when both are connected. Later commands for that session go there, even after the other browser connects. `close_session` removes the binding. A command that asks for the other browser fails with `session_browser`.

## Commands run in arrival order [#commands-run-in-arrival-order]

Each session has one queue. Commands for a session run one at a time, in the order the daemon receives them, so a click that follows a snapshot acts on the page that snapshot described. Sessions do not share a queue, and a page that responds slowly in one session does not hold another session.

`dialog` and `close_session` are answered outside the session queue, so they still reach a tab whose command is waiting. One session can have 32 commands running or waiting at once.

## New tabs open in the background [#new-tabs-open-in-the-background]

`navigate` opens a tab when the session has no current tab or the command sets `newTab`. The tab opens in the background and joins the session's tab group:

```json
{
  "session": "research",
  "action": "navigate",
  "args": { "url": "https://example.com/docs", "newTab": true, "group_title": "Research" }
}
```

- `group_title` sets the title of the group. A navigation that opens a tab can change it; otherwise the current title stays. The default is the session name.
- The group is created collapsed, so task tabs do not widen the tab strip. Expand it to look at the pages.
- A later `navigate` without `newTab` reuses the current tab. A session holds at most 32 tabs, task and borrowed together.
- `list_tabs` returns only the session's tabs, with URL, title, active flag, group title and whether the tab is borrowed.

## Borrowing one of your tabs [#borrowing-one-of-your-tabs]

`find_tab` with `active: true` claims the tab that is active in the last focused window. The URL must match exactly or by hostname:

```sh
omw call research find_tab '{"url":"example.com","active":true}'
```

Without `active: true`, `find_tab` only looks at tabs the session already holds. A borrowed tab stays open, and `close_tab` refuses it with `borrowed_tab`. The session uses it and releases it when it ends. One tab belongs to one session at a time, and another session that asks for it gets `tab_busy`. Presets apply only to tabs the session opened. Borrow a tab when the task needs the page you have open; otherwise open a task tab.

## Ending a session [#ending-a-session]

`close_session` cancels the commands still running or waiting for the session, closes the tabs the session opened, and releases the ones it borrowed, which stay open. It removes the session's browser binding and drops what the session recorded on borrowed tabs: frame selection, network entries, console output and `@e` references. Closing a tab yourself removes it from the session; the session ends only with `close_session`.

## Limits [#limits]

| Limit                    | Value                                                     |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Sessions                 | 128 per browser                                           |
| Tabs per session         | 32, task and borrowed together                            |
| Commands running at once | 128 per browser; `close_session` and `dialog` use 16 more |
| Commands per session     | 32 running or waiting                                     |
| Session name             | 1 to 96 letters (including CJK), digits, `_`, `.` or `-`  |
| `timeoutMs`              | 1 to 120000, default 30000                                |

When a limit is reached the command fails with `busy` and HTTP 429 instead of waiting. Reduce concurrency, or close sessions that are finished.

## Timeouts and uncertain results [#timeouts-and-uncertain-results]

`timeoutMs` covers the whole request, including time spent waiting in the session queue. When it runs out, or when the browser disconnects in the middle of a command, the call returns `outcome_unknown`. The action may already have reached the page: a click may have happened, a form may be submitted.

<Callout type="warn" title="Retrying after outcome_unknown">
  Observe the page before reusing a command. `snapshot`, `read_page`, the tab URL, `get` and the
  network log show what the page did. Send a command again only when the state shows the action did
  not happen, and never replay a payment, publish or submit automatically.
</Callout>

## Logins come from your profile [#logins-come-from-your-profile]

Task tabs and borrowed tabs run in your browser profile, with its cookies, sessions and logins. Sessions and tab groups organize tabs, not accounts: every session sees the same logins, and clearing cookies or site storage for one task clears them for the profile. Sign out of a site when the next task should start signed out.
